html:
The civil war of 49 to 45 BCE between Julius Caesar and the Senate party led by Pompey. It made Caesar master of Rome.

As his command in Gaul ran out, Caesar's enemies planned to put him on trial. The Senate ordered him to give up his army. In January 49 BCE he led a legion across the Rubicon, the river marking the edge of his province, saying "the die is cast". Pompey, not ready, left Italy for Greece. The war ran across the whole Mediterranean:

  • 49 BCE: Caesar beat Pompey's armies in Spain;
  • 48 BCE: after a setback at Dyrrachium he crushed Pompey at Pharsalus; Pompey was killed in Egypt;
  • 48 to 47 BCE: Caesar was trapped in Alexandria, sided with Cleopatra, then beat Pharnaces of Pontus at Zela ("I came, I saw, I conquered");
  • 46 BCE: victory at Thapsus in Africa; Cato the Younger killed himself at Utica;
  • 45 BCE: the last Pompeians lost at the Battle of Munda in Spain.

Caesar pardoned many enemies, but ruling as dictator cost him his life (see assassination of Julius Caesar).
sum: The civil war of 49 to 45 BCE between Julius Caesar and the Senate party led by Pompey. It made Caesar master of Rome.
